chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj and Umar ibn Aban, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the quickest reward for goodness is righteousness, and the quickest punishment for evil is transgression; and it suffices for a person as a fault that he looks into the faults of others while he is blind to the fault of his own self, or he hurts his companion with that which is meaningless to him, or he forbids people from that which he himself is not able to leave.

key_terms.الْبَغْيُ: Transgression or aggression, denoting exceeding bounds in evil.
key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Righteousness or piety, denoting good deeds and virtue.
key_terms.عَيْباً: A fault or defect in character.

ai.seo_question: What are the three main faults of character mentioned in this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni presents this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) as a concise ethical framework, linking the speed of divine recompense directly to the quality of one's character. The Imam identifies self-absorption in others' flaws, gratuitous social harm, and hypocrisy in leadership as critical spiritual defects, urging believers to prioritize self-accountability (muhasabah) over external criticism.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abu Abdul Rahman Al A’raj and Umar Bin Aban, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> both<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The quickest Reward for a goodness is for the righteousness, and the quickest Punishment for an evil is for the transgression; and it suffices with the person as a fault that he looks into the faults of others from what he is blind upon from the faults of his own self, or he hurts his associate with that which is meaningless, or he forbids the people from that what he himself has not capacity to leave’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from abu ‘Abd al-Rahman al-‘A’raj and ‘Umar ibn Aban from abu Hamza from abu Ja’far and Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) who have said the following: “

Of the good deeds the quickest to bring reward is benevolence and of the evil deeds the quickest to bring punishment is transgression. It is enough fault in a man to look into the faults of others and turn a blind eye to his own faults or cause pain to his associates without any good reason or forbid people from that which himself is not able to avoid.”
